units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Differentiate coronary artery disease, angina, and heart failure by identifying whether the primary description concerns vessel deposits, oxygen-related chest pain, or inadequate pumping.
units.mechanism: Coronary artery disease involves deposits in vessels supplying the heart muscle, angina is acute chest pain when too little oxygen reaches heart muscle, and heart failure is ineffective pumping that fails to meet the body's needs.

mx.cwo: Atherosclerosis is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Differentiate coronary artery disease, angina, and heart failure by' is answered as atherosclerosis rather than coronary artery disease.
Characteristic disorder description is what produces distinct circulatory-system failure mechanism, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards.

coronary artery disease is settled by running 'Distinguish intrinsic initiation of cardiac activity from external': Specialised nodal cardiac musculature intrinsically regulates normal heart activity.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Distinguish the organs of the human urinary system from the parts of a nephron, and locate the nephron as the kidney's functional unit.
units.mechanism: The human excretory system contains a pair of kidneys, a pair of ureters, a urinary bladder and a urethra; each kidney contains nephrons, whose renal corpuscle is formed by the glomerulus and Bowman's capsule and whose tubule continues through named segments.

mx.cwo: Urine leaves the bladder through the ureter, and the urethra carries urine from each kidney down to the bladder.
The renal corpuscle is the glomerulus alone, and Bowman's capsule is the first segment of the renal tubule before the proximal convoluted tubule.
The walls of the ureter and the urinary bladder are built from nephrons too, because the nephron is the functional unit of the urinary system.
The renal tubule is an organ of the urinary system, listed alongside the ureter and the urethra, because all three are tubes that carry urine.
Bowman's capsule is the fluid-filled bath surrounding the whole coiled renal tubule, into which wastes collect from the blood inside the tubule.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Classify a substance movement in the nephron as glomerular filtration, tubular reabsorption or tubular secretion by its location and direction.
units.mechanism: Urine formation has three distinct processes: the glomerulus filters blood, renal tubules reabsorb material from filtrate, and tubular cells secrete substances such as H+, K+ and ammonia into filtrate.

mx.cwo: The tubular cells secrete glucose and amino acids into the filtrate, while H+ and K+ are the substances reabsorbed into the blood.
H+ crossing the wall of the proximal convoluted tubule is reabsorption, because the proximal convoluted tubule is the reabsorbing segment.
Glucose passing from the filtrate back into the blood is tubular secretion, and K+ passing from the tubular cells into the filtrate is tubular reabsorption.
Water leaving the descending limb of Henle's loop is glomerular filtration, because filtration goes on all along the nephron.
Water moving from the medullary interstitium into the collecting duct is secretion, because the arrow points into the nephron.
H+ cannot be secreted into filtrate that is already more acidic than the tubular cells, so the acid in urine must all have come from the glomerulus.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Relate glomerular filtration rate to daily filtrate volume and use the filtrate-to-urine comparison to infer the scale of reabsorption.
units.mechanism: Glomerular filtration rate is the volume of filtrate formed by the kidneys per minute; a healthy value of about 125 mL per minute is about 180 L per day, while about 1.5 L of urine is released, implying nearly 99 per cent reabsorption.

mx.cwo: About 180 L of blood passes through the kidneys each day and 1.5 L of that blood is lost as urine.
Every healthy person forms exactly 180 L of filtrate and passes exactly 1.5 L of urine daily, so a person passing 2 L of urine has diseased kidneys.
Nearly 99 per cent of the urea in the filtrate is reabsorbed as well, since 99 per cent of the filtrate goes back into the blood.
GFR = 125 mL/min, so daily filtrate = 125 x 24 = 3000 mL = 3 L per day.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Assign reabsorption and secretion to the correct nephron segment instead of treating all tubule regions as functionally identical.
units.mechanism: The proximal convoluted tubule performs extensive reabsorption of essential nutrients, electrolytes and water and secretes H+ and NH3; the distal convoluted tubule conditionally reabsorbs Na+ and water, reabsorbs HCO3-, and selectively secretes H+, K+ and NH3; the collecting duct can reabsorb large amounts of water and also moves urea into the medulla.

mx.cwo: Nearly all the glucose and amino acids and 70-80 per cent of the electrolytes are recovered in the distal convoluted tubule, while the proximal tubule only conditionally reabsorbs Na+ and water.
The distal convoluted tubule always reabsorbs the same fixed amount of Na+ and water, so urine volume is the same whether a person is dehydrated or has drunk a litre of water.
Once filtrate has left the proximal convoluted tubule nothing more is reabsorbed, so the collecting duct only adds substances to the filtrate.
The proximal and distal convoluted tubules reabsorb equal amounts because both are coiled, while the straight limbs of Henle's loop reabsorb nothing at all.
The distal convoluted tubule reabsorbs only water and the collecting duct reabsorbs only NaCl, alternating just as the two limbs of Henle's loop do.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Distinguish the descending and ascending limbs of Henle's loop by the substance that leaves each limb and explain why filtrate concentrates during descent.
units.mechanism: Water leaves the descending limb of Henle's loop, while NaCl leaves the ascending limb; loss of water makes the filtrate more concentrated as it descends.

mx.cwo: NaCl leaves the descending limb of Henle's loop and water leaves the ascending limb.
The filtrate is at its most concentrated where it leaves Henle's loop for the distal tubule, because it has been losing water all the way round the loop.
The filtrate becomes more concentrated as it descends, and that rising concentration then pushes water out of the descending limb into the interstitium.
Water is reabsorbed only from the descending limb, so no water at all is recovered in the proximal convoluted tubule or the collecting duct.
Water leaves the descending limb only when ADH is present, so with no ADH the filtrate does not become concentrated as it descends.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Explain why opposite flows in Henle's loop and the vasa recta, rather than water removal alone, allow concentrated urine to be produced.
units.mechanism: Counter-current flow in Henle's loop and the vasa recta, together with their close proximity and NaCl and urea movements, maintains an interstitial osmolarity gradient that increases toward the inner medulla; this gradient draws water from the collecting tubule and concentrates urine.

mx.cwo: Blood in the vasa recta flows in the same direction as the filtrate in Henle's loop, and this parallel flow is what builds the medullary gradient.
Henle's loop alone maintains the medullary gradient; the vasa recta only carries blood past and plays no part in holding the solute there.
The medulla becomes concentrated because the water squeezed out of the collecting duct collects there and the solutes left behind pile up.
The interstitium is at 1200 mOsmol per litre throughout the kidney, cortex included, so water can be drawn out of the nephron anywhere along its length.
Filtrate flows out of the ascending limb straight into the vasa recta, because the two vessels are joined where they run side by side in the diagram.
The medullary interstitium must contain fewer solutes than the filtrate so that water and wastes can pass out of the collecting duct into it.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Select the kidney-regulation response that matches the initiating change in body fluid state, glomerular conditions or atrial blood flow.
units.mechanism: Kidney function is regulated by feedback involving osmoreceptors and the hypothalamus, the juxtaglomerular apparatus and the heart: excessive fluid loss activates osmoreceptor-hypothalamic signaling associated with ADH and water reabsorption, a fall in glomerular flow, pressure or filtration rate activates renin release, and increased atrial blood flow releases ANF, whose vasodilation lowers blood pressure.

mx.cwo: A fall in glomerular filtration rate triggers release of ANF from the juxtaglomerular cells to restore filtration.
Renin is released by the juxtaglomerular apparatus whenever glomerular blood pressure changes, so a rise in glomerular pressure releases renin as well.
Blood pressure falls, so ANF is released from the atria and raises the blood pressure back to normal by constricting the vessels.
The osmoreceptor and hypothalamus route works only when a person drinks water; heavy sweating does not activate it because no water has entered the body.
The question mentions a change in blood pressure, so the hormone involved is ANF, whichever site the change was measured at.
Renin is secreted from the juxtaglomerular cells into the filtrate, like H+ and K+, and acts on the filtrate as it passes down the tubule.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Order the sensory, neural and muscular events that convert bladder filling into micturition.
units.mechanism: Urine is stored in the urinary bladder until bladder stretching initiates neural signaling; the central nervous system response contracts bladder smooth muscle while relaxing the urethral sphincter, causing urine release in the micturition reflex.

mx.cwo: Urine is released when the bladder contracts and the ureters relax to let the urine back out of the body.
Urine is released as soon as the bladder smooth muscle contracts, whether or not the urethral sphincter has relaxed.
The central nervous system first sends the signal that stretches the bladder, and the stretch receptors then report back that urine has been released.
Micturition is entirely voluntary, so there are no stretch receptors in the bladder and the bladder empties only when a person decides to empty it.
Micturition happens when ADH is released, because ADH is the hormone that decides how much urine leaves the body.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Match a non-renal excretory substance to the organ and secretion through which it is eliminated.
units.mechanism: Besides the kidneys, lungs eliminate carbon dioxide and water, the liver eliminates substances through bile, and skin glands eliminate substances through sweat and sebaceous secretions.

mx.cwo: Bilirubin and biliverdin leave the body in sweat, while NaCl, urea and lactic acid are carried out in the bile.
The liver excretes bilirubin simply because bilirubin is found in the liver, and the blood excretes urea because urea is carried in the blood.
The lungs also breathe out urea and other nitrogenous wastes, so a patient with failed kidneys can clear urea by breathing deeply.
Sweat is dilute urine made by the skin, so the sweat glands are small nephrons that filter blood the way the kidney does.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Explain how haemodialysis removes nitrogenous wastes from blood when failed kidneys allow urea to accumulate.
units.mechanism: Kidney malfunction can cause harmful urea accumulation in blood; during haemodialysis, a porous cellophane membrane permits molecules to move by a concentration gradient into dialysis fluid that lacks nitrogenous wastes while retaining plasma-like composition otherwise.

mx.cwo: In haemodialysis a donor kidney is connected to the patient's blood vessels and takes over filtration of the blood.
The dialysis fluid has the same composition as normal plasma, including its usual urea content, and the machine still clears the urea from the blood.
For urea to leave the blood the dialysis fluid must contain more urea than the blood, so that the urea in the fluid pulls the blood urea across.
Because the cellophane is porous, blood cells and plasma proteins pass into the dialysis fluid too and are lost from the patient during every session.
The artificial kidney forms urine, which is drained away through a tube, because it does everything a real kidney does.
Blood is forced through the cellophane under pressure so that a filtrate forms outside the tube, and that filtrate is the dialysis fluid.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Differentiate uremia, renal calculi and glomerulonephritis by the material or structure directly affected.
units.mechanism: Uremia is the harmful accumulation of urea in blood due to kidney malfunction, renal calculi are insoluble masses of crystallised salts formed within the kidney, and glomerulonephritis is inflammation of the kidney's glomeruli.

mx.cwo: Inflammation of the glomeruli is called uremia, and a build-up of urea in the blood is called glomerulonephritis.
Any raised blood urea reading is uremia, so a healthy person who has eaten a large protein meal has uremia that day.
A patient with kidney stones has uremia, because uremia is the general name for a kidney that is not working properly.
Renal calculi and glomerulonephritis are the same disorder because both are found inside the kidney, while uremia is the one that is outside it.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Which mechanism—amoeboid, ciliary, or muscular—accounts for a movement in a given human-body context?
units.mechanism: Human cells and body parts use different movement mechanisms: pseudopodial movement is amoeboid, coordinated ciliary beating moves material through ciliated tubes, and muscle contractility moves structures such as limbs, jaws, and the tongue.

mx.cwo: Dust is cleared from the trachea by pseudopodia on the tracheal cells, so tracheal clearance is amoeboid movement.
One cilium beating on a cell is enough to move mucus up the trachea, so the cilia of neighbouring cells do not need to beat together.
Food is moved down the oesophagus by ciliary movement, because material travelling through any tube in the body is moved by cilia.
Movement of the tongue is not really movement, because the person stays in the same place while the tongue moves.
A cilium beats because actin filaments slide over myosin filaments inside it, so ciliary movement is a form of muscular movement.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: How can skeletal, visceral smooth, and cardiac muscle be distinguished from location, appearance, and control?
units.mechanism: Muscle identity depends on a combination of anatomical location, striation pattern, and control: skeletal muscle is associated with the skeleton and is striated and voluntary, visceral muscle lines hollow internal organs and is smooth and involuntary, and cardiac muscle forms the branching striated muscle of the heart.

mx.cwo: The muscle in the wall of the stomach is cardiac muscle because it is involuntary, and the branching striated muscle of the heart is smooth muscle.
All striated muscle is attached to bones, so cardiac muscle must be joined to the ribs and sternum by tendons.
The deep red muscle is cardiac and the pale muscle is skeletal, because the heart is the reddest organ in the body.
Visceral smooth muscle cannot contract because it has no sarcomeres or Z lines; it only stretches and recoils passively.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: At which structural level—fascicle, muscle fibre, myofibril, or sarcomere—does an observed skeletal-muscle feature belong?
units.mechanism: Skeletal muscle is organised hierarchically: a muscle contains fascicles, each fascicle contains muscle fibres, each fibre contains parallel myofibrils, and each myofibril contains serial sarcomeres.

mx.cwo: Each myofibril is bounded by the sarcolemma, contains sarcoplasm and many nuclei, and holds many parallel muscle fibres inside it.
The sarcomere is the anatomical unit of muscle, so a whole muscle is built directly from sarcomeres bundled together in fascicles.
Each sarcomere contains several myofibrils lying side by side between its two Z lines.
Every level has its own sarcolemma, so each myofibril and each sarcomere is separately wrapped in a sarcolemma of its own.
A myofibril is one actin filament together with one myosin filament, so a myofibril and a filament are the same level of structure.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Does a named contractile component belong to the thin actin filament or the thick myosin filament?
units.mechanism: Thin filaments are actin-based structures, whereas thick filaments are polymers of meromyosin; both filament types lie parallel to one another and to the long axis of the myofibril.

mx.cwo: Tropomyosin polymerises to form the thick filament, while meromyosin runs alongside the F-actin strands of the thin filament.
The thin filament is a single unbranched chain of actin molecules with no helical winding and no second strand.
Many F-actin molecules join together to form one G-actin filament, and two of these G-actin filaments wind round each other.
The part of an actin filament that lies inside the A band is thick filament, because the A band is where the thick filaments are.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Which geometrical changes in a sarcomere show contraction by the sliding-filament mechanism?
units.mechanism: A sarcomere contracts when thin filaments slide inward relative to thick filaments, pulling their attached Z lines inward and shortening the sarcomere.

mx.cwo: The I band is the central thick-filament-only region of the sarcomere and the H zone is the region containing only thin filaments.
This sarcomere is contracting because its I band is narrow; the H zone and the Z-line spacing do not need to be looked at.
The Z lines are pulled inward first and they drag the thin filaments along with them over the thick filaments.
At maximum contraction the thin filaments have slid right past each other, so the sarcomere length falls to zero and the Z lines meet.
A sarcomere is contracted when the whole of it looks uniformly dark, because the dark A band is where the filaments are crowded together.
The sarcomere shortens because the myosin heads themselves fold up and get shorter each time they rotate, pulling the two Z lines together.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: How are neural initiation, cross-bridge cycling, and calcium removal ordered across contraction and relaxation?
units.mechanism: A central-nervous-system signal carried by a motor neuron initiates muscle contraction; repeated cross-bridge formation, head rotation, and cross-bridge breaking sustain filament sliding, while pumping calcium ions back into the sarcoplasmic cisternae masks actin and permits relaxation.

mx.cwo: Calcium is pumped back into the mitochondria of the muscle fibre, and that is what ends the contraction.
A motor unit is one muscle fibre with its own motor neuron, so a muscle containing a thousand fibres needs a thousand motor neurons.
The muscle fibre generates the impulse and sends it back along the motor neuron to the central nervous system, which is what makes the movement voluntary.
Every fibre in a muscle contracts together whenever any signal arrives, so a muscle can only contract fully or not at all.
A muscle contracts more strongly when more ATP is present, so a well-fed muscle at rest is already partly contracted.
Relaxation happens because the thin filaments slide back out under the sarcomere's own elastic recoil, so no calcium pump is needed.
The myosin head rotates through its power stroke first and only then attaches to actin, and the cross-bridge is broken before ATP binds.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Does a bone or skeletal structure belong to the axial skeleton or the appendicular skeleton?
units.mechanism: The axial skeleton consists of the skull, vertebral column, sternum, and ribs along the main body axis, whereas limb bones and their girdles form the appendicular skeleton.

mx.cwo: The scapula lies along the main body axis and is part of the axial skeleton, while the sternum belongs with the pectoral girdle in the appendicular skeleton.
The pelvic girdle is axial because it forms part of the trunk, and only the free limb bones are appendicular.
The human skeleton has 80 bones in all, with the limbs and girdles counted inside that 80.
Flat bones such as the skull, sternum and ribs are axial and long bones are appendicular, so the short vertebrae are appendicular too.
The pectoral and pelvic girdles are joints between the limbs and the axial skeleton, so they are counted in neither the axial nor the appendicular set.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: How do pectoral and pelvic girdles map the upper and lower limbs to the axial skeleton?
units.mechanism: The pectoral girdle articulates the upper limb with the axial skeleton, whereas the pelvic girdle articulates the lower limb with the axial skeleton.

mx.cwo: The pelvic girdle is formed by the clavicle and the scapula meeting at the acetabulum, while the ilium, ischium and pubis form the pectoral girdle.
The ilium, ischium and pubis are three separate bones that never fuse, so each side of the pelvic girdle has three loose bones and the girdle has six.
Every limb attaches at an acetabulum, so the humerus fits into an acetabulum on the scapula.
The clavicle joins the sternum, which is axial, so the clavicle is an axial bone and the pectoral girdle consists of the scapula alone.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: How does the material between articulating skeletal parts determine the joint class and its movement capacity?
units.mechanism: Joint structure governs movability: cartilage joining adjacent bones permits limited movement, whereas a fluid-filled synovial cavity between articulating bone surfaces permits considerable movement.

mx.cwo: The joint between adjacent vertebrae is a synovial joint, and the shoulder is a cartilaginous joint.
Any joint with a space between the two bone surfaces is synovial, even when that space contains no fluid at all.
Only synovial joints are true joints, because a joint has to act as a fulcrum for muscle force; the contacts between adjacent vertebrae are not joints at all.
This joint is synovial because a gap is drawn between the two bone ends in the figure.
A joint crossed by large muscles is synovial and one crossed by small muscles is cartilaginous, because movement capacity comes from the muscles.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Which muscular or skeletal disorder is indicated by a stated cause and defining effect?
units.mechanism: Muscular and skeletal disorders are distinguished by the affected structure and causal pattern: neuromuscular-junction autoimmunity indicates myasthenia gravis, progressive skeletal-muscle degeneration indicates muscular dystrophy, low body-fluid calcium indicates tetany, general joint inflammation indicates arthritis, age-related bone-mass loss indicates osteoporosis, and uric-acid crystals in joints indicate gout.

mx.cwo: Progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle is tetany, while rapid muscle spasms from low body-fluid calcium are muscular dystrophy.
Any inflamed and painful joint is gout, so a patient with joint inflammation and no crystals is diagnosed with gout.
Myasthenia gravis is degeneration of the skeletal muscle fibres themselves, so it is found by muscle biopsy rather than at the neuromuscular junction.
An older patient with a painful joint has osteoporosis, because osteoporosis is the disorder of old age.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Choose neural coordination when coordination must be quick and point-to-point, and distinguish it from chemical integration through hormones.
units.mechanism: The neural system provides an organised network of point-to-point connections for quick coordination, whereas the endocrine system provides chemical integration through hormones.

mx.cwo: The endocrine system works by releasing neurotransmitters into the blood so that they can reach distant organs.
Any coordination between two organs is neural coordination, because the neural system is what connects the organs of the body.
Saliva and the digestive juices are hormones, because they are chemicals released by glands to act on another part of the body.

If the frequency of allele A doubles from 0.3 to 0.6, the frequency of AA also doubles, from 0.09 to 0.18.
In the ABO blood-group system the frequency of each of the six genotypes is simply p squared for that allele.
Genotype AA contains two A alleles, so its frequency is 2p, which is 1.2 when p equals 0.6.
With p equal to 0.6 and q equal to 0.4 the frequency of AA is p times q, that is 0.24.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Identify a departure from Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium by linking changed allele frequencies to forces that alter the gene pool.
units.mechanism: Gene migration or gene flow, genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination, and natural selection can disturb Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.

mx.cwo: When 200 individuals migrate into a population from another region, the allele frequencies change by genetic drift.
A flood that washes away half the food supply disturbs Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, because the population has been disturbed.
Only mutation can disturb Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, because only mutation actually changes the DNA.
Migration of 200 individuals cannot disturb the gene pool, because no new allele has been created in the population.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Classify stabilising, directional, and disruptive selection from how a phenotype-distribution curve changes.
units.mechanism: Stabilising selection makes the distribution peak higher and narrower, directional selection shifts the peak in one direction, and disruptive selection produces two peaks.

mx.cwo: A curve that has split into two separate peaks with a dip in the middle shows directional selection.
This curve has one tall narrow peak, so it shows stabilising selection, wherever that peak happens to sit on the axis.
The peak lies on the right-hand side of the graph, so this figure shows directional selection.
The two peaks in this distribution appeared by random genetic drift, so the figure shows no selection type at all.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Read a phylogenetic diagram by combining branch relationships with the geological time axis instead of treating it as a simple ladder of living forms.
units.mechanism: A phylogenetic tree represents the appearance and branching of animal groups through geological time, with extinct and living lineages placed by both relationship and age.

mx.cwo: Each line on the tree is a single animal that lived for millions of years and then turned into the animal at the top of its branch.
A group first appearing at 300 million years ago is younger than a group first appearing at 50 million years ago.
Reptiles are an extinct group, so the lizards and snakes alive today cannot be reptiles.
The tree shows only animals whose fossils have been dug up, so a soft-bodied lineage with no fossils has no branch and never existed.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Combine fossil age, anatomy, and behavior when ordering evidence about human evolution rather than inferring ancestry from one superficial resemblance.
units.mechanism: Evidence about human evolution is interpreted by aligning dated fossil forms with anatomical and behavioral traits.

mx.cwo: Dryopithecus was the more human-like of the two forms and Ramapithecus was the more ape-like.
A baby chimpanzee's skull looks like an adult human's, so a chimpanzee passes through a human stage as it grows up.
Dryopithecus and Ramapithecus also wore hides and buried their dead, because those are human behaviours.
Neanderthals had a 1400 cc brain, so they came after modern humans and are our most recent descendants.
Ramapithecus looked human-like only because it lived in a similar way, so its resemblance says nothing about human ancestry.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Decide whether a condition represents health or disease by considering physical, mental and social functioning rather than using absence of infection as the only test.
units.mechanism: Health is a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, whereas disease is present when the functioning of one or more organs or body systems is adversely affected and signs or symptoms appear.

mx.cwo: The temperature of 39 degrees recorded by the doctor is a symptom, and the headache the patient describes is a sign.
He runs ten kilometres a day and has no illness, so he is in complete health whatever else is going on.
Bringing the temperature down with a wet cloth cures typhoid, because the fever is what is damaging the organs.
Nobody on Earth is healthy, because no one has complete physical, mental and social well-being all the time.
She looks strong and has no visible marks on her body, so she is in complete health.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Select an infectious-disease control measure by matching it to the pathogen's route of transmission rather than to the pathogen's name alone.
units.mechanism: Prevention interrupts transmission: clean water, food and personal or public hygiene reduce contamination-based spread, avoidance of infected contact or belongings reduces contact spread, and vector control reduces insect-borne spread.

mx.cwo: Malaria is prevented by keeping away from malaria patients and not using their clothes or bedding.
Clearing stagnant water from coolers and drains has nothing to do with hygiene, since hygiene is only about clean food and drink.
A spotless air-conditioned room cannot transmit any infection, because there is nothing dirty in it.
Once you have had typhoid you need not bother about clean water again, because your body will stop the bacteria itself.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Track the malarial parasite through the correct human-host and mosquito-host stages when predicting how malaria continues to spread.
units.mechanism: A female Anopheles mosquito transfers sporozoites to a human; the parasites reach the liver through blood, reproduce, and continue through human stages before another mosquito acquires the parasite and carries the cycle onward.

mx.cwo: The mosquito injects gametocytes into the person, and these gametocytes travel in the blood to the liver.
Any mosquito bite can give you malaria, because mosquitoes carry the parasite in their saliva.
Any fever that comes with shivering is malaria, because haemozoin release is what causes chills.
The mosquito takes so much blood that the person becomes weak and feverish, and that blood loss is malaria.
The parasites multiply inside the mosquito's liver first and only afterwards pass into the human bloodstream.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Classify a defence as innate or acquired by testing for birth presence, specificity and memory.
units.mechanism: Innate immunity is a non-specific defence present at birth, while acquired immunity is pathogen-specific and characterised by memory.

mx.cwo: Interferons are the antibodies that B-cells make against a virus, which is why they are specific to it.
An allergy a child is born with counts as innate immunity, because the child had it from birth.
Skin and mucus are acquired immunity, while the antibody response after a measles vaccine is innate immunity.
Phagocytic cells and interferons are acquired immunity because they work inside the body instead of on its outer surface.
Hay fever is innate immunity, since it starts immediately on contact with pollen without any earlier illness.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Predict whether an acquired immune response will be primary or secondary from the body's history of exposure to the same pathogen.
units.mechanism: First encounter with a pathogen produces a primary response, while immune memory allows a later encounter with the same pathogen to produce a secondary response.

mx.cwo: The first infection leaves some of the germs stored in the body, and those stored germs attack the pathogen when it comes back.
Having had chickenpox gives a secondary response to measles, because the body has already responded to an infection once.
A second dose of a poison always affects the body less than the first, because the body remembers it from last time.
This patient was severely ill, so her body was mounting the secondary response, and the mild case next door was a primary one.
The second attack is milder because the skin and the phagocytes have got better with practice at keeping that microbe out.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Assign antibody production and helper activity to the correct lymphocyte type.
units.mechanism: B-lymphocytes produce antibodies in response to pathogens, while T-cells do not secrete antibodies and instead help B-cells produce them.

mx.cwo: B-lymphocytes produce antigens into the blood in response to the pathogen, and these antigens attack it.
T-cells make the antibodies and B-cells help them to do it.
Only B-cells matter in immunity; T-cells take no part in the primary or secondary immune response.
Antibodies are made by the phagocytes that swallow the germ and then release antibody made from its remains.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Infer an antibody's chain composition, connections and binding regions from its Y-shaped representation.
units.mechanism: An antibody is an H₂L₂ molecule made of two heavy chains and two light chains linked by disulfide bonds, with antigen-binding sites at the tips of the two arms.

mx.cwo: The heavy and light chains of an antibody are joined to one another by peptide bonds along the arms.
In the Y-shaped molecule the two long chains are the light chains and the two short ones are the heavy chains.
IgM and IgE are not antibodies at all; only IgG is an antibody because antibodies are the proteins that fight infection.
H2L2 means the antibody has two chains altogether, one heavy and one light, joined at the centre.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Recognise active immunity by identifying that exposure to antigen causes the host to produce its own antibodies.
units.mechanism: Active immunity develops when exposure to living or dead microbes or other antigenic proteins causes antibodies to be produced in the host body.

mx.cwo: Active immunity develops when antibodies from a dead microbe enter the host and make the host produce antigens.
A newborn given antibodies in its mother's milk has active immunity, while a child given a tetanus vaccine has passive immunity.
Only actually catching the disease gives active immunity; a killed vaccine cannot, because dead microbes are not antigens.
Anything given by injection is passive immunity and anything caught naturally is active immunity.
Active immunity is the skin and mucus actively keeping microbes out all the time.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Explain vaccination as deliberate antigen exposure that uses immune memory rather than as direct destruction of every pathogen.
units.mechanism: Vaccination introduces antigenic proteins of a pathogen or inactivated pathogen material so that immune memory can support protection on later exposure.

mx.cwo: A vaccine is a dose of antibiotic that kills the germs before they can make you ill.
Give the measles vaccine once the rash has appeared and it will cure the illness by destroying the virus.
Protection starts the instant the needle goes in, so a person vaccinated this morning is fully protected this afternoon.
The first dose of a vaccine protects against nothing, because a primary response is too weak; only the booster protects.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Distinguish an allergic response from ordinary protection by recognising an exaggerated immune response to an environmental antigen.
units.mechanism: Allergy is an exaggerated immune response to particular antigens in the environment, and those triggering substances are allergens.

mx.cwo: The allergen is the substance the body makes against the dust, and it is what produces the sneezing.
His headache goes away when he leaves the office, so he is allergic to the office.
Foods and medicines cannot be allergens, because an allergen has to be something floating in the air that you breathe in.
Sneezing at pollen is the immune system killing the germs inside the pollen grains, so hay fever is useful protection.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Classify lymphoid organs as primary or secondary by whether lymphocytes mature there or encounter trapped antigens after maturation.
units.mechanism: Bone marrow and thymus are primary lymphoid organs where immature lymphocytes differentiate, while spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer's patches and appendix are secondary lymphoid organs to which mature lymphocytes migrate.

mx.cwo: Lymph nodes are primary lymphoid organs because lymph is produced in them.
The spleen and the lymph nodes are the primary lymphoid organs, and the bone marrow and thymus are secondary.
The liver and the spleen are primary lymphoid organs, because blood cells are produced in them.
The spleen is a secondary lymphoid organ because it works during the secondary immune response, after the first infection is over.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Trace HIV replication from viral RNA entry to integration and production of new viral RNA instead of treating viral RNA as if it directly becomes part of the host genome.
units.mechanism: HIV is an RNA retrovirus whose reverse transcriptase produces viral DNA; the viral DNA incorporates into the host genome, after which the infected cell produces new viral RNA and releases replicated virus.

mx.cwo: HIV uses RNA polymerase to copy its RNA straight into the host genome.
HIV brings DNA into the cell and reverse transcriptase copies that DNA into RNA before it joins the host genome.
Every virus makes DNA from its RNA with reverse transcriptase and then joins the host genome.
Once the viral DNA joins the host genome the cell loses contact inhibition and grows into a tumour.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Identify cancerous growth as a failure of normal growth regulation and contact inhibition rather than as any instance of cell division.
units.mechanism: Normal cell growth and differentiation are highly regulated, and normal cells stop growing through contact inhibition; cancer develops when these regulatory mechanisms break down.

mx.cwo: Cancer spreads because cancer cells touch healthy cells and infect them, and that is what loss of contact inhibition means.
Only chemicals can cause cancer; radiation and viruses cannot, because they do not react with anything in the cell.
Leukaemia is not a cancer, because there is no lump anywhere in the body.
Cancer is caused by a germ, so it can be caught from a patient and cured with a course of antibiotics.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Choose whether a cancer-related method addresses causation, early detection or treatment by following what the method acts on.
units.mechanism: Carcinogens can induce neoplastic transformation; biopsy, histopathology, cancer-specific antibodies and molecular techniques can support detection; surgery, radiation therapy and immunotherapy are treatment approaches.

mx.cwo: Cancer-specific antigens are the chemicals that cause cancer by transforming normal cells.
She carries the inherited susceptibility gene, so she already has cancer and must start treatment now.
Taking a biopsy makes the cancer spread, so the needle is what turns a small tumour into a widespread one.
Radiotherapy can only cause more cancer and never treat it, because radiation is a carcinogen.
Cancer is prevented by isolating patients and keeping their belongings separate, so isolation is the main cancer-control method.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Predict the principal action of an abused drug from its drug class and biological target.
units.mechanism: Opioids bind opioid receptors in the central nervous system and gastrointestinal tract, cannabinoids interact principally with cannabinoid receptors in the brain, and cocaine interferes with dopamine transport.

mx.cwo: Cocaine acts by binding to opioid receptors in the brain and the gut, which is how it changes behaviour.
Heroin speeds the body up and makes the user energetic, while cocaine slows the body down and makes the user sleepy.
Heroin has no effect at all on the gut, because opioid receptors are found only in the brain.
Cannabis and coca both come from plants, so they act on the same receptor and produce the same effect.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Distinguish addiction from dependence by separating repeated psychological attachment from withdrawal after abrupt discontinuation.
units.mechanism: Addiction is a psychological attachment that drives repeated use, whereas dependence is revealed when abrupt discontinuation of a regular dose produces an unpleasant withdrawal syndrome.

mx.cwo: The nausea and shaking he felt after taking a very large dose is the withdrawal syndrome, so he is dependent.
Any anxiety or nausea in a drug user shows dependence, whether or not the person has stopped taking it.
Shaking and nausea after stopping the drug show addiction, while wanting to take it again shows dependence.
Alcohol cannot produce dependence, because it is legal and sold openly in shops.
A person is dependent only once the liver is damaged, so someone with normal liver tests cannot be dependent.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Predict immediate, infectious, long-term and social consequences from the pattern of drug or alcohol abuse.
units.mechanism: Drug and alcohol abuse can cause immediate reckless or violent behaviour and overdose, intravenous use increases the risk of AIDS and Hepatitis B, and chronic use damages the nervous system and liver while also causing social harm.

mx.cwo: Long-term alcohol use causes cirrhosis of the kidney, which is why heavy drinkers need dialysis.
A single use of any drug causes coma and death, because drugs stop the body working.
Anyone who smokes cannabis is at high risk of AIDS and Hepatitis B, because all drug users catch these infections.
Alcohol is a drink sold in ordinary shops, so it cannot damage the nervous system the way drugs do.
The AIDS risk comes from the drug being impure, so a pure drug injected with a shared needle is safe.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Choose prevention and support strategies for adolescent drug or alcohol risk by matching them to curiosity, peer pressure, stress and early warning signs.
units.mechanism: Drug and alcohol use during adolescence can be reduced through avoidance of undue peer pressure, education, counselling, constructive direction of energy and timely help for problems and stress.

mx.cwo: The whole prevention programme is a talk listing the medical damage drugs cause, and nothing else is needed.
The boy is anxious and under pressure from his friends because he uses drugs; stopping the drug will remove both.
Once a person is past twenty there is no point in counselling or education, because prevention only works in adolescence.
A student who dresses neatly and gets high marks needs no preventive attention at all.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Decide whether a microbe should be classified as harmful or useful from what it does, rather than assuming that every microbe is pathogenic.
units.mechanism: Microbes can cause disease, but many microbes and microbially derived products are useful to human beings, so pathogenicity is not a property of all microbes.

mx.cwo: The white patch on the plate is a single bacterium that has grown big enough to see without a microscope.
Since microbes make curd and bread, no microbe causes disease and germs are only a superstition.
The bacteria forming a visible patch on the food are harmful, because you can see how much of them there is.
Lactobacillus is not a useful microbe, because it does not make any antibiotic to cure a disease.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Given a change in a household food, identify the microbial process or product responsible for that change.
units.mechanism: Microbial fermentation can transform food, and carbon dioxide produced during fermentation causes dosa and idli dough to puff up.

mx.cwo: Curd is formed when yeast acts on the milk and ferments its sugar.
Milk turns into curd because the bacteria fill it with carbon dioxide, and the gas is what thickens it.
Curd has not been changed by any microbe, because there are no bubbles or holes anywhere in it.
Dosa dough puffs up because the yeast in it makes alcohol, and the alcohol pushes the dough upwards.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Match an industrially useful microbial product to the organism or microbial activity that produces it.
units.mechanism: Industrial microbiology obtains particular products by growing the appropriate microbe at large scale: Saccharomyces cerevisiae produces fermented beverages and commercial ethanol, while other microbes supply enzymes and bioactive molecules.

mx.cwo: Cyclosporin A is produced by Monascus purpureus and statins are produced by Trichoderma polysporum.
Only wine and beer are industrial microbial products; lipases, statins and cyclosporin A are made by chemical factories.
Lipase in a detergent packet is a manufactured chemical, not a microbial product, because it comes out of a plastic bottle.
Statins and cyclosporin A are antibiotics, since they are medicines purified from microbes.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Distinguish an antibiotic from a microbial culture and connect antibiotic production to the treatment of disease.
units.mechanism: Antibiotics are products obtained from microbes and purified for use in treating serious diseases; Penicillin was the first antibiotic discovered.

mx.cwo: Penicillin is an antibody that the mould produces against bacteria and that the patient then borrows.
Ethanol and the acid in curd are antibiotics, because they are substances produced by microbes.
The clear ring around the mould on the plate is the Penicillin, so scraping up that ring gives you the medicine.
Treating the infection means giving the patient the Penicillium mould itself so that it can attack the bacteria inside him.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Given a sewage-treatment operation, decide whether it belongs to primary physical treatment or secondary biological treatment.
units.mechanism: Primary sewage treatment removes particles by filtration and sedimentation, whereas secondary treatment uses naturally occurring heterotrophic microbes in aerated, mechanically agitated effluent.

mx.cwo: Secondary treatment uses autotrophic microbes that make their own food, so they do not consume the organic matter in the sewage.
Raw sewage with all its grit and large particles can be pumped straight into the aeration tank, since the microbes will digest everything.
Filtration and sedimentation are secondary treatment, while aeration with bacterial flocs is primary treatment.
The water is clear to the eye after settling, so it is fully treated and can be released into the river.
The aeration tank works without oxygen and its bacteria turn the sewage into methane gas.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Use biological oxygen demand and floc settling to decide when aeration is complete and what material becomes activated sludge.
units.mechanism: After biological treatment has reduced the biological oxygen demand significantly, bacterial flocs are allowed to settle, and the resulting sediment is activated sludge.

mx.cwo: A high BOD means plenty of oxygen has been supplied to the tank, so a high BOD shows the effluent is well treated.
The BOD of the effluent rises as the microbes work, so treatment is finished when the BOD reaches its highest value.
A low BOD proves the effluent contains no harmful substance of any kind and is fit to drink.
The material at the bottom of the settling tank is the sand and grit from the sewage, which is why it is thrown away.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Predict the products and destination of sludge placed under anaerobic digestion.
units.mechanism: Anaerobic bacteria digest material in sludge and produce gases including methane, hydrogen sulphide, and carbon dioxide; methane-producing microbes thereby connect sludge digestion with biogas formation.

mx.cwo: The bacteria burn the sludge inside the digester and the smoke from that burning is the biogas.
Methane is given off throughout sewage treatment, including from the aeration tank while air is being pumped through it.
The digester gas smells foul, so it is just hydrogen sulphide and cannot be burnt as a fuel.
Cattle dung has to be added to the sludge digester, because methane can only be produced from dung.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Explain how the arrangement of a biogas plant collects microbial gas and makes it available as fuel.
units.mechanism: Microbial activity in dung slurry produces a methane-rich gas mixture; the gas accumulates under a floating holder that rises and is carried through a gas outlet for use as fuel.

mx.cwo: The spent slurry is pushed out through the pipe at the top of the gas-holder and the biogas escapes from the side outlet at the bottom.
Any tank of water with a floating cover will fill with biogas, because gas always collects under a lid.
A gas-holder that is standing still means no gas at all is being made, so the plant has stopped working.
The slurry rises like dough and the gas under the holder is carbon dioxide, so biogas is mainly carbon dioxide.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Decide whether a proposed pest-control action is biological control by checking whether it uses living interactions rather than indiscriminate chemical killing.
units.mechanism: Biological control manages pests and plant diseases through natural enemies and ecological interactions, while broad chemical control can kill useful and harmful organisms indiscriminately.

mx.cwo: Trichoderma is a plant disease of the roots, and it has to be controlled by spraying a fungicide.
Pulling out the weeds by hand and covering the soil with plastic sheeting are both biological control.
Spraying neem extract is biological control, because neem comes from a plant and is a natural substance.
Adding Glomus to the field is biological control, since a living organism is being put into the soil to help the crop.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Match a biological-control agent to the organism or disease it can attack instead of treating all agents as interchangeable.
units.mechanism: Biological-control agents act through particular biological relationships: ladybirds act against aphids, dragonflies against mosquitoes, Trichoderma species against plant disease, and baculoviruses against insects and other arthropods.

mx.cwo: Release ladybirds to control the mosquitoes and dragonflies to control the aphids on the crop.
The ladybird is the pest on the crop, and aphids are released into the field to feed on it.
Spray baculovirus on the tomato crop to cure the fungal disease on its leaves.
Dragonflies are used against caterpillars because both are large, and the tiny baculovirus is used against tiny mites.
Trichoderma works because an antibiotic is extracted from it and sprayed on the leaves to kill the pathogen.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Distinguish microbial biofertiliser mechanisms by deciding whether the plant gains soil phosphorus or fixed atmospheric nitrogen.
units.mechanism: Mycorrhizal fungi such as Glomus absorb phosphorus from soil and pass it to the plant, whereas cyanobacteria such as Anabaena, Nostoc, and Oscillatoria can fix atmospheric nitrogen.

mx.cwo: Anabaena takes nitrogen out of the paddy soil and hands it to the rice plants, the way a mycorrhiza handles phosphorus.
Every bacterium and every cyanobacterium in the soil fixes atmospheric nitrogen for the crop.
Every fungus growing in the soil supplies phosphorus to the roots of nearby plants.
The fungus covering the root is taking food from the plant, so a mycorrhiza harms the crop and should be removed.
Anabaena helps a paddy field by killing the insects and pathogens in the water rather than by adding any nutrient.

units.subject: biology
units.decision_hinge: Decide whether a process is biotechnology by checking whether it uses organisms, cells, their parts, or enzymes to produce a useful product or service, and distinguish modern biotechnology by its reliance on genetic engineering and contamination-free bioprocess engineering.
units.mechanism: Biotechnology integrates natural science with organisms, cells, their parts, or molecular analogues to make useful products and services; modern biotechnology is enabled by altering genetic material and maintaining sterile conditions for large-scale production.

mx.cwo: Cells is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Decide whether a process is biotechnology by checking whether it uses' is answered as cells rather than organisms.
organisms still holds here even though Traditional microbe-mediated processes such as making curd, bread, or wine still qualify is missing from the stem.

units.mechanism: An alien DNA fragment normally fails to multiply in progeny cells unless it is associated with a vector that can replicate in the host; linkage to an origin of replication enables the attached DNA to be copied.

units.mechanism: Exonucleases remove nucleotides from DNA ends, whereas restriction endonucleases inspect DNA for a particular recognition sequence and cut both strands at specified positions within that sequence.

units.decision_hinge: Judge whether a DNA molecule is a suitable cloning vector by checking for an origin of replication, a usable selectable marker, and a preferably unique restriction site for insertion.
units.mechanism: A cloning vector must support replication through an origin of replication, permit recovery of transformed cells through a selectable marker, and provide very few, preferably one, recognition site for insertion of alien DNA.

units.decision_hinge: Distinguish transformants from recombinants by using selectable-marker survival for DNA uptake and insertional inactivation for the presence of alien DNA in the vector.
units.mechanism: A selectable marker identifies cells that received the vector, while insertion of alien DNA into a marker gene can inactivate that gene and thereby distinguish recombinant vectors from non-recombinant vectors.

The selectable marker rule also covers this: Do not accept a response that violates this limit: Selection for vector uptake distinguishes transformants, so it is not an exception.

units.decision_hinge: Select a DNA-delivery method that overcomes the recipient cell's barrier, making bacterial cells competent before heat-shock uptake or directly injecting recombinant DNA into an animal-cell nucleus.
